svg.text: Both global Clifford Thom inverse products
E → X: metric real bundle; X may be noncompact; no spin-c structure required.
CX = C₀(X); AE = C₀(E, π*Cl⁺(E)). All Clifford tensor products are graded.
1. The first product is the oscillator
bE: c⁺(v)/√(1+|v|²). dE: D = Σ(eᵢ−ιᵢ)∂ᵥᵢ on L²(Eₓ, ΛEₓ,ℂ).
Q = D + Σvᵢ(eᵢ+ιᵢ); Q² = −Δ + |v|² + 2N − r.
Connection and positivity identify the actual product; λ(Q²) = 2(|n|+k).
ker Q = ℂ·π⁻ʳᐟ⁴exp(−|v|²/2) ⊗ Λ⁰ (even, O(r)-invariant) ⇒ bEdE = 1C₀(X).
2. The reverse product is a whole-module homotopy
Start: F₀ = (D+B(z))/√(1+D²+|z|²); left coefficients u(v) use A.
Ordinary tensors: Aᵢ = aᵢ⊗1, Bᵢ = Γ⊗Lεᵢ; {Aᵢ,Bⱼ} = 0.
Even rotation Uθ: D+Bz ↦ D−Az; the coefficient action rotates A ↦ B.
Full parameter cycle: D+A(tv−z), 0 ≤ t ≤ 1; ‖χ(T±i)⁻¹‖ ≤ C/(1+|z|).
Translate v ↦ v+z: Q with coefficients u(v+z). Contract to u(z+sv), s ↘ 0.
The even Gaussian kernel carries the standard identity action: dEbE = identity of AE.
Why the linear-potential family stays valid at t = 0
Scalar potential sample only: r=1, z=2. T² = −∂ᵥ² + (tv−2)² + t(2N−1).
v
t = 0: constant 4
t = 1/2: zero at v = 4
t = 1: zero at v = 2
Compact source cutoff χ:
gradient bound + |tv−z| ≥ |z|−R₀.
3. Transfer the equivalence through the specified spin-c Morita module
mE: AE ≃ C₀(E)⊗Cr; βE = bEmE, αE = mE⁻¹dE. Both products are units.
Ordered sums: bE⊕F = bEbFCl E; dE⊕F = dFCl EdE.
The Clifford twist remains until this Morita transfer; changing spin-c data can twist by a line.
Full proofs: Lemmas 6.0a–b, Theorem 6.0c, Corollary 6.0d, Exercises 36–37. Classical method: Kasparov; Emerson §11.4.
